name: How do I protect my floors and adjacent rooms during a kitchen remodel?

mainEntity.name: How do contractors protect floors, hallways, and nearby rooms during a kitchen remodel?
mainEntity.text: How do contractors protect floors, hallways, and nearby rooms during a kitchen remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Protecting adjacent rooms is a major part of a well-run kitchen remodel. Contractors should use floor coverings, door and hallway protection, dust barriers, and clear containment between the work zone and the rest of the house. During demolition and construction, dust can travel farther than homeowners expect, especially in open-plan homes. Good protection also includes careful material staging, daily cleanup, and planned pathways for workers and deliveries. If flooring will remain in place outside the kitchen, it should be covered properly before heavy work starts. Homeowners should ask exactly what protection is included and how often barriers and cleanup will be maintained. This is especially important in luxury homes where damage to surrounding finishes can be costly to repair. Strong site protection is not an extra detail; it is part of preserving the value of the home during construction.
acceptedAnswer.description: Good contractors protect adjacent areas with floor coverings, dust barriers, containment walls, and daily cleanup. Protection methods matter because kitchen demolition and tile or cabinet work can easily damage flooring and spread dust through the home.
